judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated triggers, each defined by reference to the Swap Agreement's own defined terms; closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Defaulting Party and Affected Party definitions and with Section 4.22(c)'s subordination of trigger-event termination payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-directional payment definition; clear despite the page-break debris.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.22(c) and the Net Swap Payment definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines a regulatory designation with a self-executing rule identifying the holder; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Residual Certificates definition and Section 10.12 (Tax Matters).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.02(c) governs residual transfers; plausible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to the same subsection as the Transferee Affidavit definition, which is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any direct or indirect transfer or sale' is deliberately broad rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Ownership Interest and Permitted Transferee definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb trigger with a schedule of percentages; the doubled 'as of the as of' is a typo and the loss-table rows are OCR-damaged but the numbers remain legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on Delinquent, Current Specified Enhancement Percentage and Class M-1 Enhancement Percentage, all of which are defined consistently; it drives the Overcollateralization Target Amount stepdown.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A nine-item enumeration of the trust corpus with no general catch-all beyond 'proceeds of the foregoing', so anything omitted is arguably excluded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lists rights under the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement but not under the Bring Down Agreements, even though Section 2.02(d) requires the Trustee to enforce the Originators' repurchase obligations under those agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional trustee-identification clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and Article X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-month interest computation with an express shortfall reduction; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to Section 1.02, which does allocate those shortfalls among the REMIC Regular Interests; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long table with heavy OCR damage to the interest designations, but the pattern is mechanical and recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Uncertificated Principal Balance definition and the REMIC I/II tables in the Preliminary Statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A multi-paragraph balance definition with an express floor of zero; complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to Sections 6.05 and 6.07(c)(1)(ii), which are the loss-allocation and REMIC distribution provisions; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long series of weighted-average formulas; repetitive but each branch is fully specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the REMIC I table and the Uncertificated REMIC II Pass-Through Rate definition that builds on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enormous rate table whose OCR rendering has separated the Distribution Date column from the rate column, making several rows hard to match; some rows ('I-13-A through I-74-A' at Distribution Date 61) appear internally inconsistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table is meant to mirror the Uncertificated REMIC I Pass-Through Rate definition and the REMIC I table; the apparent row mismatches cannot be squared with that mirroring.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short excess computation plus an express non-reduction rule; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Applied Realized Loss Amount definition and Section 6.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The allocations do not add up: 93% plus 3% plus 1% to each of five classes is 101%, an arithmetic error on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The over-allocation cannot be reconciled with any voting provision that requires a percentage of Voting Rights, and the Residual Certificates definition lists exactly the five classes given 1% each.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification confined to the servicer capacity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Wells Fargo is simultaneously Master Servicer, Securities Administrator and a Servicer; Section 4.03 addresses the conflict expressly by routing Wells Fargo's termination through the Trustee, so the structure is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated agreement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It claims Exhibit R-3, the same exhibit the Saxon Assignment Agreement definition claims, so one of the two must be wrong.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the parties and exhibit form; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names 'the Seller' in the singular while the parallel Deutsche Bank Custodial Agreement definition names EMC and the Sponsor separately, a small inconsistency between two parallel definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated agreement and its amendment; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit Q-3 matches the exhibit list; consistent with the Servicing Agreement definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line party identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Bring Down Agreements definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated — 'the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider' omits both the date and the counterparties, so the instrument being defined is not actually identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing counterparty has to be reconstructed from the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex definition (Securities Administrator and Yield Maintenance Agreement Provider) and Section 4.22(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular in form but cured by naming the initial provider.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same entity is also the Swap Provider, which the Agreement nowhere flags; not a conflict but a concentration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Yield Maintenance Agreement definition and Section 4.22(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line account definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Section 5.04, which the table of contents titles 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex' rather than an account-creation provision, so the reference is at least imprecise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Yield Maintenance Agreement definition, which includes any credit support annex.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three parallel allocation waterfalls, each fully specified with pro rata rules; long but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with Current Interest, Uncertificated Accrued Interest and Section 6.02; the 98%/2% split matches the REMIC II Interest Loss Allocation Amount construct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso says 'the Seller may deliver the following documents' but every lettered sub-clause then says 'the Depositor may deliver', and clause (v) allows a lien search 'in lieu' of a title policy without saying who decides; the delivery list is the classic battleground over what a complete Mortgage File requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conveys 'the assets in the Mortgage Loans' to the Depositor while the Trust Fund definition is much broader, and the certification and repurchase machinery in Sections 2.02 and 2.03 depends on exactly what Section 2.01 required to be delivered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to appear to be defective on its face' is an open standard governing what must be excepted, and the sentence 'deliver to the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee an Initial Certification' is missing a conjunction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Initial Certification' and 'Interim Certification' are used as defined terms but neither appears in Article I, and the review is expressly narrowed for subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01 in a way that limits the Trustee's acceptance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on whether a document 'appear[s] defective on its face', an open-textured test, and imposes a duty to 'promptly notify' without a defined period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Final Certification' is likewise undefined in Article I, and the notice goes only to the Sellers even though Section 2.02(d) puts enforcement on the Trustee and Section 2.03 requires notice to all parties.
